findings.title: Nearness beyond vertical height
findings.claim: The surrounding pericope lets nearness remain relational while its later rise-and-fall choreography makes responsiveness to transmitted voice, rather than physical height alone, the measure of approach.
findings.mechanism: The focus mountain, bringing-near, and confidential-speech carriers first invite an upward spatial model. The supplied 19:57 raising and 19:58 recitation, falling, and prostration carriers then reverse the bodily direction, so the same prophetic sequence holds elevation and receptive descent together.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can keep the mountain scene's elevation while noticing that the pericope's final response approaches through hearing and submission rather than through ascent alone.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory pericope-level spatial resonance. It does not claim that the focus bringing-near verb lexically means ascent, falling, or prostration, and it does not displace the ordinary mountain setting.

epistemic.reason: The outlier has complete supplied focus and 19:57-19:58 anchors and a coherent focus return, but it is explicitly surprising and its branch records are legacy-unbound.
